claim: A rating of -1 accepted by the widened update DTO is silently reset to null: updateExif queues SidecarWrite, handleSidecarWrite writes Rating: -1 to XMP then unlocks the rating property, onDone queues AssetExtractMetadata, and validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5) returns null so asset_exif.rating becomes NULL. The same line also drops a -1 xmp:Rating authored by other tools on import.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: A `-1` rating set through the widened API is silently reset to `null` by the sidecar-write → re-extract chain

claim: Deleting the already-shipped ConvertNegativeRatingToNull migration makes Kysely's #ensureNoMissingMigrations throw 'corrupted migrations' at startup on any instance that recorded it; the throw happens before the allowUnorderedMigrations gate, runMigrations rethrows, and onBootstrap awaits it unguarded, so the server crash-loops and all later migrations are blocked.
raw: #2 🔴 Critical: Deleting the already-shipped `ConvertNegativeRatingToNull` migration makes the server fail to boot on any instance that ran it

claim: BaseSearchSchema.rating remains z.int().min(1).max(5).nullish(), feeding MetadataSearchDto, RandomSearchDto, SmartSearchDto and StatisticsSearchDto, so all four search endpoints reject rating: -1 with a 400 — a user can mark assets rejected but cannot search for them.
raw: #3 🟠 High: `-1` is settable but not searchable — the search DTOs still reject it

claim: ExifResponseSchema.rating is still z.int().min(1).max(5).nullish().default(null) and publishes minimum 1 / maximum 5 in the OpenAPI spec, yet the server will now return exifInfo.rating = -1, so any consumer validating responses against the published schema rejects a response the server considers correct.
raw: #4 🟠 High: The published response contract cannot represent the value the server will now return

claim: The diff edits this describe block but no test asserts -1 is accepted (the 'should leave correct ratings as-is' case only sends 1 and 5, and the deleted negative-rating case was not restored), and 'should reject invalid rating' tests 7, 3.5 and -2 but never 0 — so a regression widening the predicate to v >= 0 would pass the whole suite.
raw: #5 🟠 High: No test asserts `-1` is accepted, and none pins `0` as rejected

claim: Moving the rating constraint from .min()/.max() into .refine() erases the range from the machine-readable contract: z.toJSONSchema cannot see refinements, so the emitted OpenAPI and generated Dart client now show minimum -9007199254740991 / maximum 9007199254740991 for UpdateAssetDto and AssetBulkUpdateDto, and a spec-driven consumer sees 0 as in range.
raw: #6 🟡 Medium: `.refine()` erases the valid range from the machine-readable contract

claim: The published OpenAPI spec now contradicts itself about -1: the update DTOs' x-immich-history says 0 is no longer valid while all four search DTOs still say -1 is deprecated / no longer valid, and the released v2.6.0 deprecation entry is deleted rather than superseded, leaving clients who migrated off -1 with no trail explaining the reversal.
raw: #7 🟡 Medium: One published spec now contradicts itself about `-1` in four places

claim: `asset.exifInfo?.rating || null) as Rating` launders -1 through a Rating type declared as 1|2|3|4|5|null, so a rejected asset renders identically to an unrated one, the Clear rating button still shows, and handleSelect's equality guard never matches -1 so the first star click silently overwrites the reject mark.
raw: #8 🟡 Medium: Web renders a rejected asset as unrated, and a cast hides `-1` from the type system

claim: A -1 rating syncs into the mobile drift DB and yields _currentRating = -1.0, so `filled = _currentRating > index` fills no stars and `if (_currentRating > 0)` hides the clear button — rejected and unrated look identical on mobile and the reject can neither be set nor cleared there.
raw: #9 🟡 Medium: Mobile renders a rejected asset as unrated with no way to clear it

claim: The rating validity rule is duplicated inline at four sites with now-divergent rulesets — asset.dto.ts (-1,1..5,null), exif.dto.ts (1..5,null), search.dto.ts (1..5,null), sync.dto.ts (any int) — with no shared definition, unlike the file's own latitudeSchema/longitudeSchema convention; this is the root cause of findings #1, #3 and #4.
raw: P1 🟡 Medium: `rating`'s validity rule is duplicated at four sites with three now-divergent rulesets

claim: Duplicate resolution does `asset.exifInfo?.rating ?? 0` then `if (assetRating > rating)` and `if (rating > 0)`, so merging a group containing a rated and a deliberately rejected asset resolves to the positive rating and silently un-rejects it; a group where every member is -1 propagates nothing.
raw: P2 🟢 Low: Duplicate resolution treats `-1` as absent and silently un-rejects
